children: By Samantha Kroontje, Andrew Scurria and Alexander Gladstone

Optimum Communications is nearing a debt restructuring deal that would hand control of the U.S. broadband provider to its lenders and resolve ongoing litigation between them, according to people familiar with the matter.

The proposed transaction would cede equity to a group of top lenders, including Apollo Global Management, Oaktree Capital Management and JPMorgan Chase, the people said. Negotiations are ongoing and the final terms could change, they said.

A deal would also end a legal standoff that started last year when Optimum sued its creditors, the people said. Optimum alleged in the lawsuit the lenders violated antitrust laws by fixing debt prices and blocking new financing — claims the lenders denied.
Last month, creditors countersued in New York state court, accusing Optimum and its founder of fraudulently moving billions of dollars worth of assets beyond their reach.
French telecom billionaire Patrick Drahi, who owns Optimum, is largely aligned on the terms, the people said.
Creditors, advised by Akin Gump and PJT Partners, have been negotiating with the company for months to address more than $26 billion in debt. About $6 billion is due in 2027.

The company transferred key assets away from the creditors last year, court papers show. Optimum then created a new subsidiary in May that didn't secure the debt to house those assets, including its Optimum East Cable and a stake in its Lightpath commercial fiber business. It raised $300 million in preferred equity from third-party investors while Drahi swapped $200 million of his common shares for an equal amount of preferred equity.
Creditors allege in court papers that those transactions siphoned money from creditors with the intent to defraud them while enriching Drahi and other insiders.
